answer: When registrations surge like a gale, the registry answers with a spiral fee: the first hundred newcomers in an epoch pay 5 POA each, the next hundred pay 10, then 20, doubling with every hundred. A burst of 1,000 fake identities therefore costs 511,500 POA before any of them can work. Each newcomer must also finish one real job drawn from the yarrow bed of verified client tasks, checked by a peer who stakes 25 POA on the verdict; a junk job forfeits the fee and burns the checker's stake.
